facts.statement: The genus Archaeospheniscus was described by Marples in 1952.
The genus Notodyptes is a synonym of Archaeospheniscus.
The smallest species, A. wimani, was about the size of a gentoo penguin and lived 34 to 50 million years ago in Antarctica.
facts.quote: A. wimani, the smallest species (about the size of a gentoo penguin), was found in Middle or Late Eocene strata (34-50 MYA) of the La Meseta Formation on Seymour Island, Antarctica

facts.statement: The humerus of Archaeospheniscus was very slender, intermediate between ordinary bird wings and the thickened wings of modern penguins.
facts.quote: Its humerus is still very slender, between the form seen in ordinary bird wings and the thickened condition found in modern penguins.

facts.statement: It is unknown whether Archaeospheniscus is an ancestor of modern penguins or represents a case of parallel evolution.
facts.quote: Whether this signifies that the genus is an ancestor of modern taxa or represents a case of parallel evolution is unknown.

facts.statement: Archaeospheniscus lived from 41.03 to 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bartonian to Chattian (41.03 to 23.04 million years ago)
